values.note: $15 a night including tax, as the forest's own page states; the DNR's statewide table lists the first-come primitive rate at $12.15.

fees.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/jackson-washington-state-forest/ ('Primitive (class C) camping is available for $15 a night (includes tax)'), read 2026-11-02

booking.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/jackson-washington-state-forest/ ('Campers can choose from any of the sites ... available') + https://www.in.gov/dA/d3b09aa4f3/fo-JW_trail_maps.pdf ('Campers can choose from any available sites'), neither offers a reservation; the youth tent campground alone is 'by reservation', read 2026-11-02

note: Primitive campground on the hillside above Knob Lake, 2.5 miles southeast of Brownstown. Some sites are waterfront; others sit among hardwoods or eastern white pines. Firewood at the forest office in business hours, Memorial Day weekend to late October. Youth tent area and Knobstone backcountry excluded. --Claude
summary: Base $12-12.15 -> $15 (forest's own page; statewide table says $12.15, flagged). FCFS, 48-numbered sites consistent. Lakefront stands: some pads within ~10-20 m of Knob Lake. Pin on empty hillside ~180 m off.
flags: FEE CONFLICT: this forest's page says '$15 a night (includes tax)'; the statewide first-come table says Primitive $12.15. Wrote the forest's own figure, same call as Clark (1090).
PIN: 38.8663,-86.0027 sits on empty hillside. Centre of the campground ~38.8655,-86.0009, ~180 m east-southeast (leaf-off imagery shows the roads and many pads). Under 250 m; suggested nudge only.
PHONE (stored empty): 812-358-2160, forest office, DNR page. Google's campground listing 4.8 from 5; forest 4.6 from 394.

WATER: lakefront stands, and the page agrees ('Some are waterfront sites on Knob Lake'). On leaf-off imagery (0.38 m/px) the pads at the lake's northeast end come within ~10-20 m of the shore, with parked units visible. Knob Lake is 7 acres per the DNR. The rest of the loops are up the hill, and the road along the north shore is day use with docks. Overpass was down; distances are imagery estimates.
FIT: page silent on length. Trailers visible parked on gravel pads on leaf-off imagery. No rule found against RVs.
NOT STATED: toilets, drinking water, a dump and season appear nowhere on either DNR page; those stay unwritten. Site count (48) is implied only by 'sites 1 and 48'; left as is.
ADVISORIES: Skyline Drive and Mail Route Road winter closures are elsewhere on the forest; neither is the State Road 250 campground approach per the DNR text.
